item.text:
**1B.2: Nuclear rhetoric in 2024**

Bottom line: I found **no reliable 2024 evidence that Nguyễn Phú Trọng used reckless nuclear threats, brinkmanship, apocalyptic language, or language normalizing nuclear use**. What I did find was mostly **civilian nuclear-energy planning** and **non-escalatory “peace/cooperation” framing**. The closest counterevidence is Vietnam’s continued strategic closeness to Russia during the Ukraine war, but that is indirect and not nuclear rhetoric.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Metadata | Why it matters for 1B.2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Support | [Vietnam PM says arms expo is a message of peace, cooperation and development](https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-pm-says-arms-expo-is-a-message-of-peace-cooperation-and-development/2409783/) | Reuters via ThePrint; 2024-12-19 | Vietnam publicly framed defense activity as trust-building and war-prevention, and reiterated the “four no” policy. This is the clearest 2024 language I found consistent with responsible security rhetoric. `1B.2` |
| Support | [Vietnam open to using small module nuclear reactors, Politburo document shows](https://itpc.hochiminhcity.gov.vn/news/itpc/-/asset_publisher/MFd2QPqTUGF0/content/vietnam-open-to-using-small-module-nuclear-reactors-politburo-document-shows-bao-reuters-4-9-viet-nam-san-sang-su-dung-lo-phan-ung-hat-nhan-mo-un-nho-/pop_up?_101_INSTANCE_MFd2QPqTUGF0_languageId=vi_VN&_101_INSTANCE_MFd2QPqTUGF0_viewMode=print) | Reuters via Vietnamese portal; 2024-09-04 | The nuclear language I found is technocratic and civilian: small modular reactors, energy planning, and investment. It does not show threats, brinkmanship, or normalization of nuclear weapons use. `1B.2` `1B.1` |
| Support | [Vietnam to amend national power plan to include nuclear energy](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Vietnam-to-amend-national-power-plan-to-include-nuclear-energy--48116847/) | Reuters via MarketScreener; 2024-10-21 | Vietnam’s nuclear references were again about electricity supply and energy mix, not military signaling. This is relevant as absence-of-irresponsible-rhetoric evidence. `1B.2` `1B.1` |
| Weak counterevidence | [Russia’s Putin to visit Vietnam, sparking US rebuke of Hanoi](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russias-putin-to-visit-vietnam-sparking-us-rebuke-of-hanoi-3486108) | Reuters via Investing.com; 2024-06-17 | Vietnam hosted Putin and avoided a Ukraine peace summit, which suggests strategic balancing and tolerance for a war-linked partner. That weakens a purely pacific reading, but it still does **not** show nuclear brinkmanship or nuclear-threat rhetoric by Trọng. `1B.2` |
| Weak counterevidence | [Russia offers to help Vietnam develop nuclear energy, RIA reports](https://theprint.in/world/russia-offers-to-help-vietnam-develop-nuclear-energy-ria-reports/2144353/) | Reuters via ThePrint; 2024-06-24 | Russia offered civilian nuclear-power help. This shows openness to nuclear cooperation with a nuclear-armed state, but the reporting is about energy infrastructure, not weapons or threatening language. `1B.2` `1B.1` |

**Search gap**
- I searched Reuters/official coverage for direct 2024 nuclear-language patterns such as “nuclear threat,” “saber-rattling,” “normalizing nuclear use,” “apocalyptic,” and “weapons.”
- I found **no reliable 2024 Trọng-specific examples** of those behaviors.
- The available 2024 material is mostly about **civilian nuclear power** or **Vietnam’s broader foreign-policy balancing**, so the evidence for 1B.2 is mainly **absence of bad evidence plus indirect support**, not direct quotes from Trọng.
